_comment: ADR-001 eval fixtures. FROZEN inputs -- every scenario pins its asOfDate, so a
re-run next month tests the same thing as today. The seed script uses relative
dates (daysFromNow), which is why these are fixtures and not seeded matters:
a seeded matter's 'overdue' drifts daily and would silently change the test.
Matter ids are synthetic (EVAL-*) and exist in no table. The harness is
decide-only and never dispatches, so nothing here can touch matter state.
groundedFacts = the values a well-grounded decision should cite. Scored as
facts-cited / facts-available. Every value a generated message could be wrong
about is present here, which is what lets the false-claim check run without a

scenarios.description: Census overdue at 0.256 confidence + application missing + target close date passed
scenarios.rationale: Due date has passed -- the system prompt's first escalation trigger. Compounded by a low-confidence extraction the agent may not correct, and a close date already elapsed.

scenarios.description: Census received and in-review at 0.412 confidence, NOT overdue
scenarios.rationale: Data-quality escalation, not a chase. The document arrived, so a reminder is wrong; the extraction cannot be trusted and the agent must not silently correct it.

scenarios.description: S1 state, but the matter has already been escalated
scenarios.rationale: The escalation is already in the action history. Re-escalating duplicates a human hand-off; the correct action is none.

actionHistory.reason: Census overdue since 2026-07-25 at 0.256 confidence; application missing since 2026-07-30; target close date passed.

scenarios.description: Healthy matter -- all documents received at high confidence, due dates in the future
scenarios.rationale: Nothing is missing, overdue, or low-confidence. The prompt is explicit that doing nothing is a valid outcome; this is the control against escalate-everything behaviour.

scenarios.description: Document missing but due in 14 days -- too early to chase
scenarios.rationale: The prompt weighs urgency explicitly: 'something due in three weeks is not the same as something due in two days'. Nothing is blocking yet.

scenarios.description: Document missing, due in 2 days, no reminder yet -- the remind branch
scenarios.rationale: The one case where a reminder is the correct action: missing, close to due, under the cadence cap, nothing sent yet. This branch has never been exercised by anything.

scenarios.description: Document still missing after the reminder cap is reached
scenarios.rationale: The prompt's own rule: 'never send more than the configured number of reminders for a single document without escalating instead'. Three sent against a cap of three; a fourth reminder is the wrong action.

actionHistory.reason: Census still outstanding, due 2026-08-05. Reminder 2 of 3.
